messages:
Morgan (AE): FYI — Deerfield wants a short POC next week. Their engineering lead asked about onboarding a custom adapter model bundle (deerfield-llama-adapt-v2). Need compat + security answers by EOD today.
Ibrahim (SE): Which model variant exactly? Are they asking for full 70B or a quantized 14B adapter?
Morgan (AE): They said 'adapter-v2 (14B quant, q4_k_mixed)'. Also called out tokenization differences and wants to validate KV cache behavior.
Priya (Solutions Engineer): Short answer: we can serve a quantized adapter but need to validate tokenization and adapter layer mapping. Custom tokenizer usually OK if they provide vocab + merges. KV/prefix caching supported for standard attention paths, adapters might change state shape.
Ibrahim (SE): I'm kicking off an automated compatibility sweep against the bundle now. Quick command I used locally:
```
redwoodctl validate-model --bundle s3://deerfield/poc/deerfield-llama-adapt-v2.tar.gz --variant adapter --check kvcache,tokenizer
```
Output (partial): "warning: aten_op kernel mismatch on opt path" — looks like a kernel selection mismatch on our current runtime profile. Will try alternate kernel set.
Tom (ProdOps): If we need a different kernel set we can stage a canary on dedicated pool — may add ~2-4h infra work. Any blocker from your side @Ibrahim?
Ibrahim (SE): Might need a small runtime tweak and rebuild with kernel flag `--enable-opt-kernel-set=alt-1`. Will test on dev pool. If successful, should be non-invasive.
Morgan (AE): From sales side, Deerfield asked about pricing for POC and performance SLOs. They want 200ms p95 for 512-token runs. Can we commit?
Priya (Solutions Engineer): For quantized 14B on a p4d-type instance we typically hit ~120-180ms p95 depending on batching. We'll aim for 200ms but need to lock in batch config and KV caching. Cost for the POC (2 dev nodes + 1 canary) ~ estimate: $1,200/day. Can offer first 3 days free as POC concession.
Elena (Legal): Heads-up — Deerfield's security team sent a vendor questionnaire and is asking for KMS integration, data retention, and breach notification SLA items. I need their questionnaire doc to map answers. Also verify whether any models will be persisted in their VPC.
Morgan (AE): Uploaded questionnaire to the shared folder and gave Deerfield the minimal support access. Link: https://s3.company/deals/deerfield/secq.pdf
sec-bot: Security scan report ready: 3 findings — missing KMS key policy entry for service account, incomplete audit log retention policy, no E2E encryption proof for adapter artifacts.
Tom (ProdOps): KMS key policy entry is quick; Elena can we get a yes/no on supporting their HSM requirements?
Elena (Legal): We can support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private deployments. For hosted POC we can offer dedicated key workaround but enterprise HSM may require Private deployment contract. I'll flag that in answers.
Ibrahim (SE): Quick compatibility update: after applying `--enable-opt-kernel-set=alt-1` the sweep passed tokenizer + kvcache checks locally. Perf baseline looks ~140ms p95 with 1-request batching. Will run canary tomorrow on dedicated pool.
Priya (Solutions Engineer): Action items: (1) Ibrahim to run canary and confirm p95 on dedicated; (2) Tom to prepare a short-run dedicated pool and KMS policy change; (3) Elena to fill questionnaire answers and confirm HSM constraints; (4) Morgan to finalize POC pricing (3 free days then metered) and communicate SLA notes to customer.
Morgan (AE): Thanks — I'll update Deerfield with those asks and propose kickoff Tue. @Ibrahim pls ping here once canary passes so I can lock calendar. :thumbsup:
Ibrahim (SE): Will do. If anything breaks I'll post logs. For traceability I'll include the `redwoodctl validate` logs in the ticket.
Elena (Legal): I'll draft the questionnaire responses and share in the folder by EOD. If Deerfield insists on HSM in hosted we'll escalate to sales ops for Private deployment pricing.
Tom (ProdOps): I'll prep the infra and update the runbook.
Morgan (AE): Great — closing loop on this thread for now. Reopen if new blockers pop up. :white_check_mark:
